# Audit wall-clock reduction: diagnose and fix why audits take hours

## Problem statement

Item-level audits routinely take hours (measured: 4.25h for a 10-child parent) and
even single-item audits exceed 30 minutes, to the point where operators avoid
running them and release gates stall. Instrumented data from every audit log on
this host shows the cost is not one slow operation but a **long chain of slow,
serial LLM calls against a 2-slot local proxy, oversubscribed by a concurrency
ceiling of 6**, with roughly **18% of total call time producing no usable result**
(timeouts and JSON re-asks).

## Users

- **Release producer** — blocked at the `ship` audit gate, waiting hours for a re-audit.
- **Implementation agent** — cannot complete the implement skill's self-review audit within a session budget.
- **Operator** — avoids auditing, so `in_review` items accumulate unreviewed.

Example user stories:

- As a release producer, I want a single-item audit to finish in **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy so the `dev`→`main` gate is not a multi-hour stall.
- As an implementation agent, I want a parent audit with 10 children to finish in **≤ 30 minutes** so it fits one session and aborts less often.
- As an operator, I want a **reproducible measurement** of audit wall-clock so I can verify a change actually helped instead of guessing.

## Diagnosis — why audits are slow (measured)

Source: `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/*/*.log`
(465 logs, 491 distinct work items, **1,637 instrumented LLM calls, 140.8h total**).
Reproduce with the script specified in AC1.

### Call-time distribution by phase

| Context | calls | total | p50 | p90 | max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `parent` (Phase 1 parent screen) | 450 | **48.3h** | 220s | 954s | 2,705s |
| `child` (Phase 1 child screen) | 412 | **38.1h** | 227s | 633s | 1,572s |
| `verdict_reask` (JSON-contract retry) | 121 | **18.7h** | 461s | 1,466s | 2,372s |
| `phase2_deep` | 285 | 16.0h | 102s | 513s | 1,800s |
| `phase2_child` | 316 | 15.8h | 101s | 529s | 1,775s |
| `false-positive-screen` | 53 | 3.9h | 168s | 600s | 1,200s |

Median call **158s**; 76% of calls ≥ 60s; 35% ≥ 300s.

### Root causes, ranked by measured cost

1. **Phase 1 screening is 62% of all call time (86.4h).** It runs as parent
   screen → N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session, and averages
   220–227s per call for what is structurally *screening*, not deep analysis.
2. **Concurrency ceiling (6) is 3× the proxy's real capacity (2 slots).**
   `GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`.
   Six concurrent `pi` sessions queue behind two slots; the queue wait is
   charged against each call's own timeout budget, inflating p90 latency.
3. **~25h of pure timeout waste.** Calls landing exactly on a budget:
   **96 at 600s** (child-screen budget), **13 at 1,800s**, **86 at 90s**.
   Each returns a `partial` fallback that does no work and forces a later re-run.
4. **18.7h of JSON-contract re-asks.** 121 `verdict_reask` calls exist only
   because the first response was not parseable JSON — and the re-ask itself
   has p50 461s, *slower* than the call it retries.
5. **No reuse across the pipeline.** Every phase re-sends its own large prompt;
   a single edited description or touched file invalidates the content
   fingerprint and discards all prior screening work.

### Where the levers are

| Lever | Measured/expected saving | Status in code |
|---|---|---|
| Size concurrency to real slot capacity | removes queue-induced inflation + most 600s/1,800s timeout waste | ceiling hardcoded default 6 (`process_semaphore.py`); slot-status query exists but only used for *child* ceiling |
| Eliminate JSON re-asks | up to 18.7h of 140.8h | `_reask_json_array_once` exists as the fallback; parse robustness not hardened |
| Batch Phase 1 parent+children into one call | collapses N+1 screens to ~1 | `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2 only, off by default |
| Route Phase 1 to a fast model | Phase 1 is 62% of time, low-reasoning work | `phase1_model` plumbing exists but **no CLI/env surface**; tiered-model item was demoted |
| Adaptive timeout + degrade early | converts 25h of dead time into fast partials | fixed 600s/1,800s budgets |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reproducible measurement harness committed.** A script (e.g.
   `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py`) parses `Per-call timing:` lines from
   `~/.audit_debug/` and prints the per-context table above (calls, total, p50,
   p90, max, and count-at-budget). Running it on this host reproduces the
   baseline numbers in this brief within expected variance, and it is covered by
   a unit test with a fixture corpus.
2. **Baseline is recorded and a target is set.** The measured baseline
   (1,637 calls / 140.8h / 62% Phase 1 / 18% wasted) is committed to
   `docs/dev/` and a small-item audit wall-clock target of **≤ 10 minutes**
   (healthy proxy, no concurrent audits) is stated and used as the regression gate.
3. **Concurrency ceiling is sized to real capacity.** The audit runner derives
   its parallel-call ceiling from the live slot status (`available_slots` /
   `total_slots`) with a safe floor, never exceeding that capacity, and falls
   back to the static ceiling when the query fails. Unit tests prove: 2-slot
   proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2; failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit
   `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` remains authoritative.
4. **JSON-contract re-asks are substantially eliminated.** Parse robustness is
   hardened (strict schema instruction, tolerant extraction, single retry only
   on genuine failures) and a regression test proves a well-formed model
   response is never re-asked. Measured `verdict_reask` count drops to ≤ 2% of
   calls in a re-measurement on the same corpus.
5. **Phase 1 call count is reduced.** Parent + child Phase 1 screening is
   batched and/or routed to a faster model so a 10-child parent issues
   materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls; a test proves the call count for a
   10-child parent is reduced versus the current N+1 structure, with no change
   to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict semantics or the
   ready-to-close gate.
6. **Post-change measurement demonstrates the reduction.** Re-running the AC1
   harness after implementation shows overall audit LLM wall-clock reduced by
   **≥ 50%** on a representative audit, with no increase in `partial`-fallback
   rate and no relaxation of any closure criterion.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, the audit skill reference, and
   `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` (or a superseding report).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics are frozen:** no change may relax the ready-to-close gate;
  a `partial` fallback must never degrade to `met`. Correctness outranks speed.
- **Do not simply raise timeouts.** The historical 900→1200→1800s bumps masked
  the inefficiency; this work reduces actual work, not the ceiling.
- Only **2 local proxy slots** exist — any parallel design must be safe below
  saturation, and must not starve interactive `pi` sessions.
- The runner is a `[READ-ONLY AUDIT]` except the already-documented persistence,
  lifecycle, and ruff-remediation exceptions — no new state mutations.
- Changes land on `dev` only; full suite must be green at the push gate.

## Existing state

- Prior epics `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` (Phase 2 perf, P1–P6) and P7
  (`SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD`) are **complete** and moved the bottleneck from Phase 2
  to Phase 1; that is now confirmed by measurement (§Diagnosis).
- Existing reports: `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`.
- Existing levers already in code but not effective by default: `--batch-phase2`,
  `phase1_model` plumbing, child-verdict reuse, content fingerprint gate,
  per-phase checkpoints.
- Related open items: `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` (simplify audit freshness) and
  `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` (queue/concurrency tuning, done but ceiling remains 6).

## Desired change

A measurable, repeatable audit performance programme: (1) lock in the harness and
baseline, (2) size concurrency to real slot capacity, (3) eliminate JSON re-asks,
(4) collapse Phase 1 call count via batching and/or a fast Phase 1 model, and
(5) re-measure to prove ≥ 50% wall-clock reduction — decomposed into child work
items during the plan stage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, `_call_pi`, timeout
  and parallelism resolution, `_reask_json_array_once`, batch-mode gates.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — concurrency ceiling default (6).
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — slot-status query reused for the ceiling.
- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new measurement harness (AC1).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling-from-slots tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — re-ask elimination tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — Phase 1 call-count tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — **Audit skill: reduce audit wall-clock time (audits far too slow)** (completed). This is the closest prior attempt and shares the same problem statement. It delivered the content freshness gate, gated child cascade, and scoped code-quality scan — **partial overlap**. This item is deliberately scoped to the *residual* drivers those levers did not remove (Phase 1 = 62% of call time, concurrency ceiling 6 vs 2 real slots, JSON re-asks, ~25h of timeout waste), plus the measurement harness needed to prove any future change is real. It does not re-do the freshness/cascade/scoping work.
- `SA-0MSADWWH3003N82D` — Audit skill Phase 2 performance evaluation and improvement (complete).
- `SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD` — Phase 1 performance treatment (P7) (complete).
- `SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE` — audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling tuning (complete; ceiling still 6).
- `SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0` — simplify audit freshness invalidation (open).
- `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL` — audit reliability RCA (reliability, not latency).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-phase1-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md`,
  `docs/dev/audit-phase2-measured-report.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `audit`, `speed up`, `Phase 2`, and all prior Phase 1/2 performance items.
One partial overlap found (`SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S`, completed) — its delivered ACs
(freshness gate, child-cascade opt-in, scoped code-quality scan) are **not** the
same as this item's ACs, and re-measurement shows the problem persists. Scope
rewritten to the residual gaps only; recorded above under Related work. One
accidental duplicate created during this intake (`SA-0MVF1GHVX008Q66T`) was
closed as a duplicate of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the logged `Per-call timing` corpus is representative; it is
  derived from this host's real audit history (491 items) and is the only
  latency evidence available.
- **Risk (quality):** batching Phase 1 into fewer, larger calls could reduce
  verdict quality — mitigated by keeping per-AC verdict semantics and comparing
  verdict output before/after on a fixed item set.
- **Risk (contention):** a parallel design sized to slots could still contend
  with interactive sessions — mitigated by a floor of 1 and never exceeding
  `available_slots`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** adjacency to freshness simplification
  (`SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0`) and the merge-gate work — those stay separate items;
  this epic links rather than absorbs them.
- **Risk (measurement):** historical numbers were taken under concurrent audit
  load; targets must be re-measured clean-room for a fair comparison.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Is the complaint about *all* audits or a specific class (single-item vs
  multi-child parent)?
  **Answer (operator, seed prompt):** "Audits take far too long" — general.
  Diagnosis shows both are affected: single-item ~10–30 min, 10-child parent
  4.25h. Scope therefore covers both, with the parent case as the primary target.
  Source: seed prompt `/intake` request; evidence: per-context table above.

- **Q:** Should the fix raise timeouts or reduce actual work?
  **Answer (derived from prior art):** Reduce actual work. Prior bumps
  (900→1200→1800s) are documented as masking inefficiency
  (`docs/dev/audit-phase2-performance-evaluation.md` §1). Source: repo docs.

- **Q:** Is switching off the local proxy (to a remote model) acceptable?
  **Answer (OPEN QUESTION — producer decision):** assumed *permitted but not
  required*; the plan prefers fast/local routing and treats remote routing
  (e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash`) as an option to confirm. Source: this intake;
  needs producer confirmation at plan review.
data.title: Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

# Audit performance measurement harness and committed baseline

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an operator or release producer, I want a committed, reproducible measurement of
audit LLM call timing, so I can verify that a performance change actually helped
instead of guessing.

## Problem statement

Every audit log on this host contains `Per-call timing:` lines, but no committed tool
parses them. The parent brief's baseline (1,637 instrumented calls, 140.8 h total,
62 % of call time in Phase 1, ~18 % wasted on timeouts and JSON re-asks) was produced
ad hoc and cannot be reproduced or regression-gated.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (parent):** `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` is committed. It parses
  `Per-call timing:` lines from `~/.audit_debug/` (configurable root) and prints the
  per-context table with columns: context, calls, total, p50, p90, max, and
  count-at-budget. Running it on this host reproduces the parent brief's baseline
  figures within expected variance (documented tolerance).
- **AC1 (parent):** The harness is covered by a unit test using a small fixture corpus
  of synthetic debug logs — the test is written before the parser logic (TDD) and
  asserts each aggregate column including the count-at-budget buckets (600 s, 900 s,
  1,800 s).
- **AC2 (parent):** `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` records the measured
  baseline (calls, total hours, per-context breakdown, Phase 1 share, wasted share)
  together with the reproduction command and a stated single-item audit wall-clock
  target of **≤ 10 minutes** on a healthy proxy with no concurrent audits, which
  becomes the regression gate.
- **AC2 (parent):** The baseline document names the gate explicitly and is referenced
  from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.
- The harness is read-only: it never writes to `~/.audit_debug/`, `.worklog/`, or the
  audit runner.
- UK English throughout.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` against a fixture corpus
   (5–8 synthetic logs spanning each context) — asserts table shape and aggregates.
2. Implement `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` with `--root`, `--context`,
   `--at-budget` CLI options and stable table output.
3. Run it on this host; record the output in `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md`
   with the mandated ≤ 10 min target and reproduction command.
4. Link the baseline doc from `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` — new harness
- `scripts/tests/test_measure_audit_performance.py` — new unit tests + fixture logs
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — new baseline + target document
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — link to the baseline document

## Dependencies

None — this is the foundation slice; every other child depends on it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the recorded `~/.audit_debug` corpus is representative (491 items,
  one host). The document records the host, date range and per-context counts so a
  different corpus is obviously different.
- **Risk:** debug logs may be pruned during the work; the fixture corpus makes the unit
  test independent of live logs while the baseline document pins the snapshot.
data.title: Audit performance measurement harness and baseline

# Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent or release producer, I want the audit runner's parallel-call
ceiling to match the proxy's real slot capacity, so calls do not queue behind slots and
inflate their own timeout budget into avoidable 600 s / 1,800 s caps.

## Problem statement

`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` defaults to 6 (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) while
`GET /llama/local/status` reports `total_slots: 2`, `available_slots: 0`. Six concurrent
`pi` sessions queue behind two slots; queue wait is charged against each call's timeout,
inflating p90 and pushing calls onto their budget (96 calls at 600 s, 13 at 1,800 s).
Slot-status querying already exists (`skill/audit/scripts/scan.py`) but is only used for
the *child* ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC3 (parent):** The audit runner derives its parallel-call ceiling from live slot
  status (`available_slots` / `total_slots`) with a safe floor of 1, never exceeding
  reported capacity.
- **AC3 (parent):** When the slot query fails or times out, the runner falls back to the
  configured static ceiling (current behaviour preserved).
- **AC3 (parent):** An explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` value remains authoritative — it
  is never silently overridden by slot discovery.
- **AC3 (parent):** Unit tests prove all three behaviours: 2-slot proxy ⇒ ceiling ≤ 2;
  failed query ⇒ configured fallback; explicit env var ⇒ that exact value.
- The ceiling derivation is logged once per run (slot status, derived ceiling, source)
  so the decision is observable in the audit log.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing concurrency tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` (mock slot status).
2. Add a `_resolve_audit_ceiling()` helper in `audit_runner.py` that queries slot status
   (reusing the existing `scan.py` query), clamps by floor 1 and `total_slots`, and
   honours an explicit `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.
3. Route every ceiling consumer through the helper (parent and child paths).
4. Log the derivation once per run; update the constant docstring in
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` to describe the derivation rather than a bare 6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling resolution and consumers
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — existing slot-status query to reuse
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — ceiling default documentation
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — ceiling behaviour section

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG child 1):
  the change must be measured before/after with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (contention):** a slot-derived ceiling could still contend with interactive
  sessions. Mitigated by the floor of 1 and never exceeding `available_slots`.
- **Assumption:** `available_slots` is a trustworthy signal for admission; the fallback
  path keeps the runner functional when it is not.
- **Constraint:** do not raise timeouts to compensate — this change reduces queueing,
  not the budget.
data.title: Size audit concurrency ceiling to real proxy slot capacity

# Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As an implementation agent, I want a well-formed model response to be accepted on the
first call, so audit wall-clock is not spent re-asking — and the re-ask itself (p50
461 s, slower than the call it retries) is not billed twice.

## Problem statement

121 `verdict_reask` calls cost 18.7 h (13 % of all measured call time) and exist only
because the first response was not parseable JSON. `_reask_json_array_once` is the
fallback path; parse robustness is not hardened, so genuine-but-unusual formatting
(fenced blocks, prose prefix, trailing commas) triggers a full second call.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC4 (parent):** Parse robustness is hardened — a strict schema instruction is added
  to the prompt, tolerant extraction handles fenced ```json blocks and prose-prefixed
  JSON, and a single retry is attempted **only** on genuine failures (no parseable
  array found, or failed schema validation).
- **AC4 (parent):** A regression test proves a well-formed model response is never
  re-asked (the retry path is not invoked when the first response parses).
- **AC4 (parent):** Additional regression tests cover fenced blocks, prose-prefixed
  JSON, and trailing-comma tolerance — each accepted without a re-ask.
- **AC4 (parent):** A re-measurement on the same corpus shows `verdict_reask` at ≤ 2 % of
  all calls (currently ~7.4 %), recorded in the baseline document's successor report.
- Verdict semantics are unchanged: no response that would previously have been re-asked
  and then rejected may now be silently accepted with different semantics; the
  `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` vocabulary and the ready-to-close gate are frozen.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing tests first in
   `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py`: well-formed ⇒ no re-ask;
   fenced ⇒ parsed; prose-prefixed ⇒ parsed; trailing comma ⇒ parsed; genuinely
   unparseable ⇒ exactly one re-ask.
2. Harden `_extract_json_array` (tolerant extraction) and add an explicit JSON-schema
   instruction to the Phase 1 prompt template.
3. Gate `_reask_json_array_once` on genuine failure only; count re-asks in the
   `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY`.
4. Re-run the measurement harness and record the re-ask share.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — prompt template, `_extract_json_array`,
  `_reask_json_array_once`, reliability summary
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` — new tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — JSON contract section
- `docs/dev/audit-performance-baseline.md` — re-measurement record

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1) — the ≤ 2 % claim must
  be measured with the committed harness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (correctness):** tolerant parsing could accept malformed verdicts. Mitigated by
  schema validation after extraction and by keeping the retry for genuine failures.
- **Constraint:** verdict semantics are frozen (parent brief §Constraints).
data.title: Eliminate JSON-contract re-asks

# Reduce Phase 1 screening call count

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As a release producer, I want a 10-child parent audit to issue materially fewer serial
Phase 1 calls, so the dominant 62 % cost centre stops dominating wall-clock.

## Problem statement

Phase 1 runs as one parent screen plus N child screens, each a fresh full-prompt session
averaging 220–227 s — 86.4 h of the measured 140.8 h. `--batch-phase2` exists for Phase 2
only and is off by default; `phase1_model` plumbing exists but has no CLI/env surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC5 (parent):** Parent and child Phase 1 screening is batched and/or routed to a
  faster model so a 10-child parent issues materially fewer serial Phase 1 calls than
  the current N+1 structure.
- **AC5 (parent):** A test proves the Phase 1 call count for a 10-child parent is reduced
  versus the current N+1 structure (asserted against a fake `_call_pi` call counter).
- **AC5 (parent):** A CLI/env surface exists for the Phase 1 model
  (`--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL`), defaulting to current behaviour so no
  existing invocation changes model silently.
- **AC5 (parent):** There is **no change** to `met`/`unmet`/`partial`/`adjusted` verdict
  semantics or to the ready-to-close gate; a batching on/off comparison on a fixed item
  set is recorded showing equivalent verdicts.
- Full `skill/audit/tests/` suite passes.

## Minimal implementation (vertical slice)

1. Write the failing call-count test first
   (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py`): a 10-child parent under batching
   issues fewer `_call_pi` invocations than the N+1 baseline, and verdicts are unchanged.
2. Extend the existing `--batch-phase2` flag family with `--batch-phase1` (default
   preserving current behaviour until the comparison evidence exists), reusing the
   Phase 2 batching machinery.
3. Expose `--phase1-model` / `AUDIT_PHASE1_MODEL` on the existing `phase1_model` plumbing.
4. Record a fixed-item-set verdict comparison and the call-count delta.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Phase 1 screening, batch gates, model selection
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase1.py` — new call-count and parity tests
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — new flags
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — Phase 1 batching and model routing

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the measurement harness + baseline child (child 1).
- Independent of the concurrency-ceiling and JSON-re-ask children, but should land after
  them so the remaining Phase 1 cost is measured on an un-inflated baseline.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (quality):** batching into fewer, larger calls could reduce verdict quality —
  mitigated by the fixed-item-set parity comparison and keeping per-AC verdicts.
- **Risk (default change):** enabling batching by default without parity evidence would
  violate the frozen-semantics constraint; the flag therefore defaults to current
  behaviour until the comparison is recorded.
- **Assumption:** a fast Phase 1 model is permissible; the remote-model option remains an
  OPEN QUESTION for the producer (parent brief Appendix) and is not required by this item.
data.title: Reduce Phase 1 screening call count

# Post-change measurement: verify ≥ 50 % wall-clock reduction

**Parent:** SA-0MVF1NKZQ009P3ZG — Audits take too long: investigate and speed up

## Goal (user story)

As a release producer, I want a post-change measurement proving the audit wall-clock
reduction is real, so the epic closes on evidence rather than assertion.

## Problem statement

Individual levers each claim savings; nothing proves the combined effect, and the parent
brief requires ≥ 50 % reduction with no increase in `partial`-fallback rate and no
relaxation of any closure criterion.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC6 (parent):** Re-running the AC1 harness after all code children land shows overall
  audit LLM wall-clock reduced by **≥ 50 %** on a representative audit, measured
  clean-room (no concurrent audits) and compared against the committed baseline.
- **AC6 (parent):** The `partial`-fallback rate has not increased versus the baseline.
- **AC6 (parent):** Every closure criterion is unchanged — the report states explicitly
  that no ready-to-close rule was relaxed, with the diff (none) shown.
- A single-item audit completes within the ≤ 10 minute target on a healthy proxy.
